content.title: Everything fans need to know about the 2026 March Madness tournaments
content.text: March 8, 2026Updated March 23, 2026, 1:20 p.m. ETThe 2026 March Madness tournament began after Selection Sunday on March 15.Men's games will be broadcast across CBS, TNT, TBS, and TruTV, while women's games will be broadcast across the ESPN family of networks.This article details the schedule, TV, tickets, gear and more about the upcoming men's and women's March Madness tournaments.The madness is here! It took getting to day four of the NCAA Tournament for the last perfect bracket to say goodbye, thanks to Tennessee upsetting Virginia, according to the NCAA.Whether you filled out a bracket for fun, watch every game religiously, or are even attending a game in person, here is everything you need to know about the March Madness tournament:When is March Madness 2026?The 2026 March Madness tournament kicked off after the 68-team bracket was revealed on Selection Sunday. The tournament will continue through March, ending with the Final Four on Saturday, April 4 and the National Championship game on Monday, April 6.Shop 2026 March Madness Final Four ticketsWhere is the March Madness tournament being held this year?Depending on the round, the 2026 March Madness has different host sites. However, Indianapolis is the main host for the men's tournament, hosting the Final Four and the National Championship. Here's a look at the men's tournament locations:First Four: UD Arena in Dayton, OhioFirst & Second Rounds: Buffalo, N.Y., Greenville, S.C., Oklahoma City, Portland, Ore., Tampa, Fla., Philadelphia, San Diego and St. Louis.Sweet 16 & Elite 8: Houston, San Jose, Calif., Chicago, and Washington, D.C.Final Four & National Championship: Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis - Shop tickets nowThe women's tournament is organized slightly differently, where teams act as host sites until the Sweet 16. No. 5 Texas TechHow to watch the most March Madness gamesMarch Madness games tend to air across TNT, TruTV, TBS, and CBS. Without cable, you will need a subscription to watch March Madness games. Sling carries TNT, TBS and TruTV in the Sling Blue package, which is the USA TODAY Shopping recommendation to watch the most games throughout the tournament. If you're also interested in the women's tournament, that usually airs entirely on the ESPN suite, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU and ESPNews. You can get all of those channels with the Sling Sports Extra add-on to your Sling Blue package.Watch March Madness games live with Sling BlueLive stream CBS March Madness games on Paramount+ or FuboCan you buy March Madness tickets already?Yes. Tickets are available now on StubHub. But, all we know right now is when games are taking place, and where. It will be a mad dash for tickets from the bracket reveal to post-game when the next round and opponent are confirmed.Shop men's 2026 March Madness ticketsMarch Madness 2026 key dates for the women's tournamentSunday, March 15: Selection SundayMarch 18-19: First FourMarch 20-21: First roundMarch 22-23: Second roundMarch 27-30: Fort Worth regionalMarch 27-30: Sacramento regionalApril 3: Final FourApril 5: National ChampionshipShop 2026 women's Final Four ticketsWhere to stay for March MadnessYou always have options when you travel, one of them being where you stay. This will depend on which city you're heading to, maybe you'll want to be in the mix of things in downtown near the arena, or maybe in a less urban space in one of those smaller college towns (looking at you, Greenville). The USA TODAY Shopping team has curated some hotel options for you, depending on where you're headed.Where to stay in Dayton, Ohio for March MadnessDayton, Ohio is going to host the first two games of the March Madness tournament, on March 17 and March 18.
